title: ChatGPT Now Has Ads: Should You Upgrade From Free to Go or Plus?
description:
This video breaks it down: after OpenAI's September 23 announcement that ChatGPT ads are live in Taiwan, which of Free, Go, and Plus can show you ads, and how Free users can choose ad-free in Settings. Then, with three questions and the NT$ monthly prices OpenAI's site lists for Taiwan, it works out step by step what each of the four paths costs a year, so you can judge for yourself whether upgrading pays off. I'm not here to pick a plan for you.

OpenAI's own Go plan page says the plan may include ads; a guaranteed ad-free experience only starts at Plus and up. Free lets you go ad-free for no money under Ad Controls in Settings, in exchange for a lower usage limit. Using the NT$ monthly prices OpenAI listed for Taiwan (checked September 25, 2026, including 5% VAT), this video works out how much a year it costs to guarantee no ads, and shows how to check the math yourself using the USD price, exchange rate, and VAT.

Yearly cost for all four paths (monthly price × 12; check the actual checkout screen):
・Free default: NT$0, ads may appear
・Free ad-free: NT$0, no ads, lower limit
・Go: NT$270 × 12 = NT$3,240, OpenAI says ads may appear
・Plus: NT$690 × 12 = NT$8,280, OpenAI guarantees no ads

My take: upgrading just to avoid ads isn't worth it. The money worth spending is for a higher usage limit and a better model — losing the ads is just a side effect.

hfr3.text: Think upgrading to Go means no more ads on ChatGPT?

8fs2.text: Or have you already seen ads under your chats?

sf4i.text: In late September, ads started appearing on ChatGPT in Taiwan.

6h4r.text: Both Free and Go may show ads.

wuun.text: Among paid plans, only Plus and up guarantee no ads.

zu2v.text: So how do Free and Go really differ, and is upgrading worth it?

nk4a.text: This video walks you through three questions to find out.

f29v.text: So what actually happened this September?

8y2j.text: Let's start with how the ads rolled out.

ntdx.text: On September 23, OpenAI made it official.

irnq.text: Ads in ChatGPT started rolling out in Taiwan.

ck4m.text: The same day, six Southeast Asian markets got them too.

mvyr.text: Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam.

z5a2.text: Taiwan wasn't singled out for testing.

5sq8.text: This rollout just happened to reach us now.

da3h.text: If you're on Free or Go in Taiwan, you may have seen one.

9mmy.text: Ads usually appear below the answer, labeled sponsored.

j6fd.text: OpenAI stresses that ads are kept separate from answers.

uz5f.text: Seeing an ad doesn't mean the answer was tampered with.

wnbp.text: Ads didn't just appear overnight; OpenAI rolled them out in stages.

jm85.text: It took OpenAI over half a year to go from a small test to global.

kbhy.text: Step one: a small US test in February.

kkaf.text: Back then, only logged-in US adults saw them.

rnkh.text: Step two: in August, it expanded to the UK, Japan, South Korea and more.

avty.text: OpenAI watched the data before expanding each time.

ny5e.text: Step three: a September 23 announcement added Taiwan and Southeast Asia.

bena.text: Taiwan is neither the first batch nor the last.

97p6.text: Looking at this timeline, I don't think ads will suddenly vanish.

s44h.text: In other words, the ad you saw has been tested for months.

228y.text: OpenAI spent months building toward this; I'd guess it only grows.

zffm.text: That paying automatically means no ads.

mq35.text: Even paying users fall for this one.

t4tf.text: Let's look at what actually separates Free from Go.

hwwr.text: Everyone knows Free may show ads.

d9he.text: But few know Free actually gives you a choice.

mni7.text: In Free's settings, you can choose to go ad-free.

zjwi.text: The catch: turning ads off means a lower usage limit.

6rsj.text: Many users don't even notice this option.

am2h.text: What about the paid Go plan?

th7i.text: Go may still show ads — OpenAI says so itself.

yd6e.text: Many assume paying to upgrade removes the ads.

63sh.text: And Go doesn't even have an ad-free option.

krra.text: To get rid of the ads, you only have two ways.

5zhe.text: Switch back to Free's ad-free setting, or upgrade further.

2wc7.text: To guarantee no ads, you need to go up to Plus.

bzae.text: So paying for Go doesn't actually buy you an ad-free experience.

2r7j.text: That's exactly where the confusion lies.

s6bb.text: I pulled this line straight from OpenAI's Go page.

id32.text: This isn't news coverage — it's OpenAI's own wording.

cuwu.text: It's written in English, right in the Go plan description.

pqey.text: In plain words: this plan may include ads.

9zvm.text: "May include" means ads might show up, or might not.

7x9h.text: It's not "may have no ads" — it's "may include ads."

ufzu.text: That phrasing leaves OpenAI plenty of wiggle room.

2csg.text: OpenAI never promises Go will be ad-free.

nsdk.text: What you're paying for is higher message, upload, and image limits.

wjbn.text: Whether Go drops ads later, OpenAI hasn't said.

ybzn.text: So your money doesn't buy a guarantee of no ads.

qkqb.text: So how do you actually judge if it's worth upgrading?

9vv6.text: Start by asking yourself three questions, one at a time.

2iw4.text: Question one, the most basic: who even sees ads?

bkve.text: Question one: check whether you see ads at all.

etc7.text: First, is your account Free or Go?

y75y.text: Plus and above are guaranteed ad-free by OpenAI.

wssi.text: This surprises a lot of people the first time.

44tt.text: Second, is your account 18 or older?

wj34.text: Accounts OpenAI judges to be under 18 won't be shown ads.

85kr.text: Third, ads are kept separate from ChatGPT's actual answer.

g7e2.text: OpenAI says ads don't change what the model tells you.

y9a8.text: In other words, seeing an ad doesn't lower answer quality.

xf4s.text: Once you know where you stand, you'll know if you need to keep going.

hbvx.text: Question two: what does turning off Free's ads cost you?

4w53.text: Here's the key point: going ad-free costs no money.

b633.text: First, the default: Free with ads.

njtm.text: Message limits are standard, and image generation works fine.

m8kh.text: In short, it's the setup you already know.

t8m4.text: And what happens after you go ad-free?

8iyr.text: OpenAI hasn't said by how much, but it does go down.

6e88.text: Tools like image generation and deep research get disabled too.

9t69.text: A lot of people rely on these two regularly.

iez3.text: If you rarely use those tools, going ad-free costs you little.

6tzc.text: But if you rely on them daily, the cost adds up.

fxs4.text: So going ad-free means no ads, but fewer features too.

5p96.text: In other words, free isn't the same as costless.

sqeq.text: The cost just isn't money — it's your usage limit.

a4qz.text: Free is never truly free, just a different currency.

d8iw.text: Question three, and today's main event: the math.

wccc.text: Let's compare all four paths and their yearly cost.

qber.text: In this table, I suggest checking the last column first: ads or not.

y7sz.text: The NT$ prices are what OpenAI listed for Taiwan in late September.

dbba.text: I multiplied by 12 for the year; your checkout screen has the real number.

3k6b.text: The four paths range from fully free to a fixed monthly charge.

cjrt.text: Path one: default Free — costs absolutely nothing.

6nku.text: This is where most people are right now.

idt6.text: Path two: Free set to ad-free — also free of charge.

dcx6.text: Ads disappear, in exchange for a lower limit.

7jze.text: A lot of people don't even know this path exists.

9hmr.text: Path three: Go, priced at NT$270 a month in Taiwan.

ds5u.text: Just over NT$3,200 a year, but OpenAI says ads may still show.

zngn.text: You pay, but get no guarantee.

y3xm.text: Path four: Plus, priced at NT$690 a month in Taiwan.

v3vc.text: About NT$8,300 a year, and OpenAI guarantees no ads here.

4vai.text: Plus costs about 2.5x Go, but at least OpenAI guarantees no ads.

688a.text: This math walks through the Go example.

8hyr.text: Add that tax, and it's about NT$268.

7pr3.text: OpenAI's listed Go price for Taiwan, tax included, is NT$270.

mjth.text: About the same as many subscriptions on your phone.

pdwh.text: The full comparison table and official links are in the article linked at the top of the description.

xjr7.text: Want to adjust it yourself? The setting isn't hard to find.

wpyz.text: The whole process takes about thirty seconds.

wwyd.text: You'll find this menu on the app or the web.

a4xx.text: It's usually bottom-left, or next to your avatar.

qmz5.text: It has "Ad" right in the name, easy to spot.

cuxx.text: Step three: if you're on a Free account.

fgax.text: You'll see an option to switch to Ads-Free.

h36w.text: Tap it, and it warns your limit will drop before you confirm.

92jv.text: Step four: if you're on a Go account.

ugxh.text: Same page, but you can only manage ad personalization.

iq9t.text: Mainly, you can choose whether ads match your interests.

6b6m.text: There's no option to turn ads off entirely.

yu7z.text: Whichever account you have, this page is worth checking once.

inhb.text: After running these numbers, what's my take?

a6vv.text: My take: upgrading just to avoid ads isn't worth it.

tk9u.text: First, Free already lets you go ad-free for nothing.

xbum.text: Most people who just want no ads don't need to upgrade.

gkia.text: The cost: a lower usage limit and fewer features.

5jce.text: Second, the plan that truly guarantees no ads is Plus.

n7g7.text: When we decide about upgrading, we should keep those two apart too.

xvyc.text: So, is upgrading actually worth it?

2kvp.text: This video isn't here to pick a plan for you.
